Rejected on artistic grounds, 2026-08-28. The issue asked to persist the variant seed to localStorage so the 10-25 MB payloads become deterministically cacheable. Tate: variety across visits IS the point of having recorded each park several times — Hartford Beach has 16 variants, Sica Hollow 6 — and a persisted seed freezes a walker onto one recording of each park permanently. That trades the work away for a cache hit.

What shipped in PR #77 instead: the seed stays per-session and unpersisted (unchanged behaviour), but moved into src/audio/variantSeed.ts where the session memo is documented as the correctness property it is — prefetch and the active load ask for the seed separately, and a different answer between them would download one recording on approach and play another on arrival. The strip now shows 'recording 2 of 6', which tells a walker there ARE others and invites the return visit the variety exists for.

Closed as a documented decision by Tate, 2026-09-05: the AAC-derived FLAC is the archive of record for Good-Earth-2-001. No calibrated rerender.

WHY, rather than 'not worth it'. The 2024 render cannot be reproduced. The project that encoded the corpus is not on this machine — conversion.RPP references 2 edits where the deliveries need 33, and Spotlight finds no other REAPER project with more than a handful of VVOctoEncode instances outside 'Veins of the Earth', a different piece from 2025. Rendering the ICEBrk session through VVOctoEncode as it stands today reproduces W at r=0.94 and nothing else: first order uncorrelated with the corpus, second order 9 to 24 dB out depending on which of the three OM-0368 calibrations is used, and none of them is the one that made the corpus. Normalization, rotation, channel order, sample rate, group delay, plugin build and codec were each tested and eliminated — see rl-dqc.7.2.

So a rerender would not restore the 2024 encoding. It would substitute a different one.

AND IT WOULD COST MORE THAN IT FIXED. pickAssetFamily serves FLAC to Safari and AAC to everything else. Rerendering only the lossless family would split the two families for this recording: iPhone walkers on a 2026 encode, everyone else on the 2024 one, for the same 60 seconds. Rerendering both would replace a delivery that is correct with one that is merely current.

This is deliberately NOT the Fort Sisseton precedent (rl-ijl), where a today-encode was accepted. That was new material with no existing counterpart, and both families were built from the same new render, so every walker hears the same thing. Here there is an existing correct delivery to lose.

WHAT THE WALKER ACTUALLY GETS: the full 2646016 samples of the right recording at the right offset, carrying AAC generation loss in the family that is nominally lossless. One file out of 102. The pair no longer throws at merge (rl-74x.1), the corpus audit passes on all 408 files, and nothing about the walk is broken.
